_about: medengine-STUDY v0.7 content. jg = Jargon Decoder (opaque eponyms and non-visual exam labels only). f = 4K film (never contains the label), h = phonetic/shape collision hook, x = exam trap, m = 1st-line move or lethal contraindication (Mode 3 strike). ck_dual rewrites existing clinchers into the dual-code format; ck_add adds new ones. UK guidance.

jg.f: Short PR (<120 ms), then the QRS starts with a slow, slurred ramp before it shoots up, so the whole complex is wide.
jg.h: Capital Δ is a triangle: its sloping side IS the slurred ramp climbing into the QRS.
jg.x: Negative Δ waves mimic pathological Q waves (pseudo-infarct): check the PR before you call an old MI.
jg.m: WPW with AF: NEVER AV-node blockers (adenosine, verapamil, diltiazem, β-blockers, digoxin); unstable → synchronised DC cardioversion; definitive cure = catheter ablation of the accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent).

jg.f: The PR gets longer, longer, longer… then a P wave arrives with no QRS after it, and the cycle resets.
jg.h: 'Weak Back' carrying a heavy PR box: each step he sags lower until he drops it, then picks it up and starts again.
jg.x: Fixed PR then a sudden dropped beat = Mobitz II: below the AV node and dangerous (risk of asystole).
jg.m: Usually benign (athletes, inferior MI, AV-nodal drugs): observe and stop AV-nodal blockers; Mobitz II or complete block → pacing.

jg.f: A young person taking deep, slow, heaving, sighing breaths, blowing off acid as CO₂, breath smelling of pear drops.
jg.h: 'Mauled by a bear': the deep, exhausted gasps of someone who has been fighting (the acid) for hours.
jg.x: Kussmaul's SIGN is a different thing: the JVP rises on inspiration (constrictive pericarditis, tamponade).
jg.m: DKA (JBDS): IV 0.9% sodium chloride first, then fixed-rate IV insulin 0.1 units/kg/h; monitor and replace K⁺.

jg.f: Fresh plaques appear exactly along a scratch, surgical scar or tattoo line on otherwise clear skin.
jg.h: 'Knife-scratch': wherever the skin is cut, a line of plaques follows the blade.
jg.x: Not specific to psoriasis: also lichen planus, vitiligo and viral warts.
jg.m: Treat the psoriasis: potent topical steroid + vitamin D analogue (e.g. calcipotriol) first line for trunk and limbs (NICE).

jg.f: Scrape the silvery scale off a plaque and tiny pinpoint bleeding spots appear underneath.
jg.h: Aus-'spitz' = spits: pull the scale and the skin spits pinpoints of blood from the capillaries just below.
jg.x: Pinpoint bleeding under silvery scale points to psoriasis, not eczema; a scaly ring with a clearing centre is tinea (scrape for fungal microscopy).
jg.m: Potent topical steroid + vitamin D analogue; screen for nail pitting and psoriatic arthritis (PEST questionnaire).

u: Acute coronary syndrome / MI / unstable angina
jg.f: Low blood pressure, distended neck veins and quiet, distant heart sounds after chest trauma or a few days after an MI.
jg.h: Three B's: Big neck veins + Beat muffled + BP low.
jg.x: Tension pneumothorax also gives low BP + raised JVP, but with tracheal deviation and an absent, hyper-resonant side; tamponade has clear lungs.
jg.m: Cardiac tamponade: urgent echo → pericardiocentesis; no diuretics or nitrates (they drop preload further).

jg.f: A head-injured patient whose BP is climbing with a widening pulse pressure while the pulse slows and breathing turns irregular.
jg.h: 'Crushed brainstem': high BP + slow pulse + irregular breaths.
jg.x: A late sign of imminent coning, not an early one; nothing to do with Cushing's syndrome (cortisol).
jg.m: Emergency: airway, head up 30°, urgent CT + neurosurgery, mannitol or hypertonic saline; NO lumbar puncture.

jg.t: Cullen's sign vs Grey Turner's sign
jg.f: Blue-purple bruising around the belly button, or along both flanks, in someone with severe epigastric pain going through to the back.
jg.h: Cullen = Centre (umbilicus); Grey Turner = Turn them on their side to see the flanks.
jg.x: Both mean blood tracking from the retroperitoneum: late and not specific (also ruptured AAA; Cullen's also ruptured ectopic).
jg.m: Severe pancreatitis: aggressive IV fluids, analgesia, Glasgow-Imrie score, HDU; ultrasound for gallstones; no routine prophylactic antibiotics.

jg.f: Two fingers under the right ribs, the patient breathes in and suddenly catches their breath and stops in pain; the same on the left does nothing.
jg.h: 'Mid-inspiration must-stop': the breath halts as the hot gallbladder slides down onto your fingers.
jg.x: Biliary colic = pain under 6 h, no fever, usually no positive sign; cholecystitis = over 6 h + fever + raised WCC + positive sign.
jg.m: Ultrasound abdomen; IV antibiotics + analgesia; laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis (NICE).

jg.f: Pressing on the left lower abdomen makes the pain flare in the right lower abdomen.
jg.h: Rovsing = Reverse: press left, it hurts right.
jg.x: Psoas sign (hip extension hurts) = retrocaecal appendix; every sign is less reliable in children, the elderly and pregnancy.
jg.m: Pregnancy test in women of child-bearing age, then laparoscopic appendicectomy with antibiotics.

jg.f: A yellow but completely pain-free patient with a smooth, non-tender gallbladder you can feel under the right ribs.
jg.h: Courvoisier = 'Cancer, Very silent': painless jaundice + a palpable gallbladder is NOT stones.
jg.x: Stones scar and shrink the gallbladder so it rarely distends: think pancreatic head cancer or cholangiocarcinoma.
jg.m: Over 40 with jaundice → suspected pancreatic cancer pathway (2WW, NICE NG12); CT pancreas protocol.

jg.f: Fever with rigors, yellow skin and right upper quadrant pain, all at once.
jg.h: Char-'hot': Hot (fever) + yellow (jaundice) + RUQ pain.
jg.x: Add hypotension + confusion = Reynolds' pentad (septic shock). Charcot FOOT is a different thing: a hot, swollen, painless neuropathic diabetic foot.
jg.m: Sepsis 6 with IV antibiotics → urgent biliary drainage (ERCP).

jg.f: Painful red lumps on the pads of the fingers, or flat painless red spots on the palms and soles, in a feverish patient with a new murmur.
jg.h: Osler = 'Ouch-ler' (painful pads); Janeway = Just flat, painless (palms and soles).
jg.x: Osler's nodes are immune-complex (painful); Janeway lesions are septic micro-emboli (painless). Both are uncommon: absence never rules out endocarditis.
jg.m: 3 sets of blood cultures from separate sites BEFORE antibiotics, then echo (TTE → TOE); modified Duke criteria.

jg.f: A tuning fork placed on the mastoid then beside the ear, and then in the middle of the forehead, asking which sounds louder and which side hears it.
jg.h: Rinne = 'Ring in the air' (a normal ear hears it louder in air); Weber = Web in the middle (the forehead fork).
jg.x: Conductive loss: Rinne negative (bone > air) and Weber goes TO the bad ear. Sensorineural loss: Rinne still positive and Weber goes AWAY to the good ear.
jg.m: Formal audiometry; unilateral sensorineural loss → MRI internal auditory meatus (acoustic neuroma); sudden sensorineural loss → same-day ENT.

jg.f: Tapping over the front of the wrist, or holding both wrists fully flexed for a minute, brings tingling into the thumb, index and middle fingers.
jg.h: Tinel = Tap-tingle; Phalen = Fold-hand (fold the wrists and hold).
jg.x: Median nerve: the little finger is spared (that is ulnar). Thenar wasting is a late sign that pushes towards surgery.
jg.m: Carpal tunnel: wrist splint at night or steroid injection; nerve conduction studies if unclear or before surgery; decompression if severe or wasting.

jg.f: After neck surgery, a BP cuff pumped above systolic makes the hand cramp into a flexed-wrist claw, and tapping in front of the ear twitches the corner of the mouth.
jg.h: Trousseau = Tourniquet claw; Chvostek = Cheek-tap twitch.
jg.x: Trousseau's sign OF MALIGNANCY is different: migratory thrombophlebitis (pancreatic cancer). Chvostek's can be positive in normal people.
jg.m: Hypocalcaemia (parathyroids injured at thyroidectomy): severe or symptomatic → IV calcium gluconate; check magnesium and PTH.

jg.f: The depth in millimetres that a melanoma has grown down into the skin, measured under the microscope.
jg.h: Breslow = 'Breadth-low': how LOW it has dug.
jg.x: It is the single most important prognostic factor; ABCDE and the ugly duckling are for spotting a melanoma, not for prognosis.
jg.m: Suspicious lesion → 2WW; excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin first, then wider excision guided by the depth.

jg.f: Brown-black pigment from a streak under the nail spreading out onto the skin of the nail fold.
jg.h: Hutch-in-son: the pigment escapes out of its hutch (the nail) onto the fold.
jg.x: The OTHER Hutchinson's sign: shingles vesicles on the tip of the nose = nasociliary nerve = the eye is involved → urgent ophthalmology.
jg.m: Pigment spreading onto the nail fold → 2WW (subungual melanoma); nose-tip shingles → oral antivirals + same-day eye review.

jg.f: Gentle sideways pressure on red skin makes the top layer slide off like a wet tissue, leaving raw, weeping skin.
jg.h: Nikolsky = 'Nick-slide': nick it and the skin slides.
jg.x: Positive in SJS/TEN, pemphigus vulgaris and staphylococcal scalded skin; negative in bullous pemphigoid (tense blisters).
jg.m: SJS/TEN: stop the culprit drug now, admit to a burns unit or ITU, supportive care; skin failure means fluid, heat and infection loss.

jg.f: Head turned 45° and the patient laid back fast with the head hanging over the couch edge: after a few seconds the eyes twist and beat and the room spins, then it settles.
jg.h: Hallpike = Hang-back: the head hangs back off the couch.
jg.x: It DIAGNOSES BPPV; the Epley manoeuvre TREATS it. Vestibular neuronitis = continuous vertigo for days with no positional trigger.
jg.m: BPPV: Epley manoeuvre (Brandt–Daroff exercises at home); vestibular sedatives like betahistine don't help BPPV.

jg.f: A whole half of the face droops, forehead included, with painful blisters in the ear canal or on the outer ear.
jg.h: Ramsay HUNT = Hunted by shingles: the virus hiding in the ear's nerve.
jg.x: Bell's palsy and this are both lower motor neurone (forehead affected); the ear vesicles and pain mean VZV and a worse prognosis.
jg.m: Oral aciclovir/valaciclovir + prednisolone within 72 h; tape the eye shut at night and lubricate.

jg.f: Hip flexed to 90°, straightening the knee triggers back pain and resistance; lifting the head forward makes the hips and knees flex by themselves.
jg.h: Kernig = Knee (can't straighten it); Brudzinski = Bend the neck, bend the knees.
jg.x: Both have poor sensitivity: a negative sign never rules out meningitis, so don't let it delay antibiotics.
jg.m: Hospital: IV ceftriaxone + dexamethasone (add amoxicillin if Listeria risk); community: IM/IV benzylpenicillin only for suspected meningococcal disease, without delaying transfer.

jg.f: Blood that sits still, blood that clots too easily and a damaged vessel wall: the three ingredients that build a clot.
jg.h: Three V's: Velocity low (stasis) + Vessel wall injury + Viscosity up (hypercoagulable).
jg.x: It is a risk framework, not a sign. Virchow's NODE (left supraclavicular, gastric cancer) is a different thing.
jg.m: Suspected PE: Wells score → CTPA (or D-dimer if unlikely); interim apixaban or rivaroxaban if the scan is delayed (NICE NG158).

jg.f: Comparing protein and LDH in the tapped chest fluid against the blood, to tell leaky-vessel fluid from inflamed-pleura fluid.
jg.h: Light = Lab ratios: fluid/serum protein >0.5 or LDH >0.6 = exudate (the heavy, inflamed fluid).
jg.x: Use it when the fluid protein is borderline (25–35 g/L). Transudate = heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic; exudate = infection, cancer, PE.
jg.m: Ultrasound-guided diagnostic tap (protein, LDH, pH, glucose, MC&S, cytology); infected fluid with pH <7.2 → chest drain.

jg.f: Short, thin, horizontal white lines at the edges of the lungs just above the costophrenic angles on a chest X-ray.
jg.h: Kerley B = Borders and Bars at the Base: fluid filling the little septa between lobules.
jg.x: One letter of the heart failure film ABCDE: Alveolar oedema (bat wings), kerley B lines, Cardiomegaly, upper lobe Diversion, Effusions.
jg.m: Acute pulmonary oedema: sit up, oxygen if hypoxic, IV furosemide; NICE: don't routinely give opiates or nitrates.

jg.f: A smoker with proximal leg weakness that briefly gets stronger with repeated effort, a dry mouth and absent reflexes.
jg.h: Lambert–Eaton = 'Lift-Easier': strength gets easier with repeated lifting.
jg.x: Myasthenia gravis is the opposite: weakness worsens with use and starts in the eyes. LEMS = antibodies to presynaptic calcium channels.
jg.m: CT chest to find small cell lung cancer; treating the tumour treats the weakness.

jg.f: One upper eyelid droops a little, that pupil is small, and that side of the face doesn't sweat.
jg.h: Horner = Horns down: lid droops, pupil shrinks, sweat dries (Ptosis, Miosis, Anhidrosis).
jg.x: Partial ptosis + SMALL pupil = this; complete ptosis + BIG pupil, eye down and out = third nerve palsy.
jg.m: Find the cause: CXR/CT for an apical (Pancoast) tumour; sudden painful onset with neck pain = carotid dissection → urgent CT angiography.

jg.f: After years of acid, the flat squamous lining of the lower oesophagus is replaced by stomach-type columnar cells.
jg.h: Barrett's = Barrier re-tiled: acid forces the oesophagus to re-tile itself with gut cells.
jg.x: Raises the risk of ADENOcarcinoma (lower third), not squamous cell carcinoma.
jg.m: High-dose PPI + endoscopic surveillance; dysplasia → endoscopic therapy (resection or radiofrequency ablation).

jg.f: Multiple, recurrent ulcers far down the duodenum with chronic diarrhoea, still not healing on a standard PPI.
jg.h: Zollinger–Ellison = Zillions of acid: a gastrin-secreting tumour pumping acid nonstop.
jg.x: Linked to MEN1 (check calcium and pituitary). Measure fasting gastrin off the PPI.
jg.m: High-dose PPI; fasting gastrin ± secretin test; localise the gastrinoma for resection.

jg.f: Draw a line across the anus: external openings behind it curve round to a midline internal opening; openings in front run straight in.
jg.h: Goodsall = Go straight in front, curve gently behind.
jg.x: Anterior openings far from the anus (>3 cm) can break the rule. Multiple or complex fistulae → think Crohn's.
jg.m: MRI pelvis to map the track; fistulotomy or seton; an acute abscess needs incision and drainage.

jg.f: A young woman with pelvic infection now also has right upper quadrant pain from string-like adhesions over the liver capsule.
jg.h: Fitz-Hugh = Fits up High: the pelvic infection climbs high to the liver.
jg.x: LFTs are usually normal; don't misdiagnose it as cholecystitis. Chlamydia or gonorrhoea.
jg.m: Treat as PID (BASHH): IM ceftriaxone 1 g single dose + oral doxycycline + metronidazole for 14 days.

jg.f: A red, scaly, crusting patch that starts on the tip itself and spreads out onto the areola, not settling with creams.
jg.h: Paget's = Patch on the Point: it begins on the nipple tip.
jg.x: Eczema starts on the areola and spares the nipple; this starts ON the nipple. Not Paget's disease of bone.
jg.m: 2WW breast referral → triple assessment (examination, imaging, punch biopsy): there is usually an underlying cancer.

jg.f: A man with buttock and thigh claudication, impotence and weak femoral pulses on both sides.
jg.h: Leriche = Leg + Libido lost: one high blockage starves both.
jg.x: Buttock claudication with absent femorals = aortoiliac disease, not a calf (femoropopliteal) problem.
jg.m: ABPI + duplex or CT angiography; best medical therapy (statin, antiplatelet, stop smoking, supervised exercise), then revascularise.

jg.f: Leg raised to empty the veins, pressure on the groin, then stand up: the veins stay empty until the pressure is released.
jg.h: Trendelenburg = Tourniquet test: block the groin to find the leaky valve.
jg.x: The Trendelenburg SIGN is different: the pelvis drops on the opposite side when standing on the weak leg (hip OA, gluteus medius weakness).
jg.m: Duplex ultrasound is the real test; endothermal ablation is first-line treatment (NICE CG168).

jg.f: Hard, bony lumps on the finger joints nearest the tips, or on the middle knuckles, with a squared-off thumb base.
jg.h: Heberden = High (the tip joints, DIP); Bouchard = B comes before H (the middle joints, PIP).
jg.x: RA hits MCPs and PIPs with soft, warm swelling and spares the DIPs; hard DIP nodes = osteoarthritis.
jg.m: Exercise and weight loss are core; topical NSAID for knee OA, oral NSAID + PPI at the lowest dose; NICE: don't routinely offer paracetamol or weak opioids alone.

jg.f: Voices discussing the patient in the third person, thoughts being put in, pulled out or broadcast, and feeling controlled from outside.
jg.h: Schneider = Snatched mind: thoughts snatched, inserted and broadcast.
jg.x: Strongly suggestive but not diagnostic: also in mania, drug-induced and organic psychosis. ICD-11 needs at least 1 month.
jg.m: Early intervention in psychosis team; oral antipsychotic + CBT for psychosis + family intervention; baseline weight, ECG, glucose and lipids (NICE CG178).

jg.f: A heavy drinker who is confused, staggering on a wide base, with eyes that jerk and can't move properly.
jg.h: Wernicke = Wobbly + Wandering mind + Wonky eyes (ataxia, confusion, ophthalmoplegia).
jg.x: Only a minority have all three: don't wait for the full triad. Untreated → Korsakoff's (memory loss + confabulation). Wernicke's APHASIA is unrelated.
jg.m: IV Pabrinex (high-dose thiamine) now, before or with any glucose.

jg.f: A patient secretly injects insulin or contaminates their urine sample, with nothing to gain except being cared for as a patient.
jg.h: The Baron of tall tales: invents illness for the sick role.
jg.x: Factitious = intentional for the sick role; malingering = intentional for external gain (money, sick note); somatisation = not intentional.
jg.m: Non-confrontational approach, one named clinician, avoid unnecessary tests; if a child is the patient (fabricated or induced illness) → safeguarding.

u: Retinal artery occlusion & sudden vision loss
jg.f: Swinging a torch from the good eye to the bad eye, the bad pupil dilates instead of constricting.
jg.h: Marcus Gunn = the Gun misfires: the light goes in and the pupil fires the wrong way.
jg.x: Means optic nerve or severe retinal disease (optic neuritis, CRAO, large detachment); a cataract does NOT cause it.
jg.m: Find the cause: painful colour loss → optic neuritis (urgent eye/neurology, MRI); sudden painless loss + cherry-red spot → CRAO on the stroke pathway.

jg.f: A young boy climbs up his own thighs with his hands to get up from the floor, with bulky calves.
jg.h: Gowers = Go up the legs.
jg.x: Means proximal muscle weakness (Duchenne); the calves look big but are fat and fibrous (pseudohypertrophy); CK is massively raised.
jg.m: CK + genetic testing; paediatric neurology referral.

ck_dual.12: 🎬 Short PR (<120 ms) + slow slurred ramp at the start of a wide QRS 🟰 🏷️ **Delta (Δ) wave** [Δ = triangle ramp] → 🎯 **WPW** (Bundle of Kent): never AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF
ck_dual.31: 🎬 Painful red lumps on the finger pads + flat painless spots on palms and soles + splinters + pale-centred retinal bleeds 🟰 🏷️ **Osler's nodes** + **Janeway lesions** + **Roth spots** [Osler = Ouch; Janeway = Just flat] → 🎯 infective endocarditis: 3 blood cultures + echo
ck_dual.32: 🎬 Tapped fluid protein >0.5 × serum or LDH >0.6 × serum 🟰 🏷️ **Light's criteria** [Light = Lab ratios] → 🎯 **exudate** (infection, cancer, PE)
ck_dual.76: 🎬 One droopy lid + small pupil + dry half-face + shoulder and arm pain in a smoker 🟰 🏷️ **Horner's syndrome** [Horns down] → 🎯 **Pancoast tumour** at the lung apex
ck_dual.78: 🎬 Plethoric, swollen face + distended neck veins, worse when both arms are raised 🟰 🏷️ **Pemberton's sign** [Put 'em up: arms up, face floods] → 🎯 **SVC obstruction**
ck_dual.110: 🎬 Lower oesophageal lining re-tiled from squamous to columnar after years of acid 🟰 🏷️ **Barrett's oesophagus** [Barrier re-tiled] → 🎯 endoscopic surveillance for **adenocarcinoma**
ck_dual.121: 🎬 Openings behind the anus curve round to the midline; openings in front run straight in 🟰 🏷️ **Goodsall's rule** [Go straight in front, curve behind] → 🎯 predicts the **fistula** track (MRI maps it)
ck_dual.142: 🎬 RUQ pain **>6 h** + fever + raised WCC + breath catches when you press under the right ribs 🟰 🏷️ **Murphy's sign** [Mid-inspiration must-stop] → 🎯 **acute cholecystitis**
ck_dual.144: 🎬 **Painless jaundice + smooth, palpable, non-tender gallbladder** 🟰 🏷️ **Courvoisier's law** [Cancer, Very silent] → 🎯 not stones: **pancreatic head cancer**
ck_dual.145: 🎬 RUQ pain + fever/rigors + jaundice 🟰 🏷️ **Charcot's triad** [Char-hot] → 🎯 **ascending cholangitis**
ck_dual.146: 🎬 Charcot's three + **hypotension + confusion** 🟰 🏷️ **Reynolds' pentad** [Really red-flag: 3 + shock + confusion] → 🎯 septic shock from obstructed bile: **urgent ERCP**
ck_dual.150: 🎬 Bruising around the umbilicus or along the flanks 🟰 🏷️ **Cullen's** [Centre] / **Grey Turner's** [Turn on the flank] → 🎯 retroperitoneal haemorrhage: **severe** disease
ck_dual.162: 🎬 PID + **RUQ pain** from string-like adhesions over the liver capsule 🟰 🏷️ **Fitz-Hugh–Curtis syndrome** [Fits up High] → 🎯 perihepatitis: treat as **PID**
ck_dual.228: 🎬 Deep, sighing, heaving breaths + pear-drop breath + abdominal pain in a young diabetic 🟰 🏷️ **Kussmaul breathing** [Mauled by a bear] → 🎯 **DKA**
ck_dual.239: 🎬 **Hot, swollen, red, painless foot** in a neuropathic diabetic 🟰 🏷️ **Charcot foot** [not Charcot's triad] → 🎯 offload in a cast; urgent foot team
ck_dual.242: 🎬 Bulging, staring eyes or waxy swollen shins in a hyperthyroid patient 🟰 🏷️ **Graves' disease** [the Grave stare] → 🎯 autoimmune (TRAb), not a toxic nodule
ck_dual.243: 🎬 **Painful tender goitre after a viral illness + raised ESR + low uptake** 🟰 🏷️ **de Quervain's thyroiditis** = subacute [Quervain = Quivering sore neck] → 🎯 NSAIDs ± β-blocker; antithyroid drugs don't help
ck_dual.294: 🎬 Hard bony lumps at the fingertip joints (DIP) and middle knuckles (PIP) + squared thumb base, MCPs spared 🟰 🏷️ **Heberden's** [High: DIP] + **Bouchard's** [B before H: PIP] **nodes** → 🎯 **hand OA**, not RA
ck_dual.304: 🎬 Climbing BP with a **wide pulse pressure** + slowing pulse + irregular breathing 🟰 🏷️ **Cushing's triad** [Crushed brainstem] → 🎯 **impending herniation**
ck_dual.342: 🎬 Voices discussing you in the third person; thoughts put in, pulled out or broadcast; feeling controlled 🟰 🏷️ **Schneider's first-rank symptoms** [Snatched mind] → 🎯 points to **schizophrenia**
ck_dual.379: 🎬 Confused + staggering + jerking, stuck eyes in a heavy drinker 🟰 🏷️ **Wernicke's encephalopathy** [Wobbly, Wandering, Wonky eyes] → 🎯 **IV Pabrinex** now
ck_dual.419: 🎬 The depth in mm that the melanoma has invaded 🟰 🏷️ **Breslow thickness** [Breadth-low: how low it dug] → 🎯 the key **prognostic** factor
ck_dual.420: 🎬 **Ugly duckling** lesion, or a nail streak whose pigment spreads onto the nail fold 🟰 🏷️ **Hutchinson's sign** [pigment escapes its hutch] → 🎯 **2WW**
ck_dual.469: 🎬 **Nail pitting, onycholysis** + new plaques along a scratch or scar 🟰 🏷️ **Koebner phenomenon** [Knife-scratch] → 🎯 **psoriasis**
ck_dual.478: 🎬 Skin slides off with gentle sideways pressure + mucosal sores after a new drug 🟰 🏷️ **Nikolsky sign** [Nick-slide] → 🎯 **SJS/TEN**: stop the drug, burns unit
ck_dual.484: 🎬 **Facial palsy + painful vesicles in the ear canal** 🟰 🏷️ **Ramsay Hunt syndrome** [Hunted by shingles] → 🎯 VZV: aciclovir + prednisolone
ck_dual.485: 🎬 **Brief vertigo (<1 min) on rolling in bed or looking up** 🟰 🏷️ **Dix–Hallpike** positive [Hang-back test] → 🎯 **BPPV**: Epley manoeuvre
ck_dual.562: 🎬 Swinging the torch to the bad eye, its pupil dilates instead of shrinking 🟰 🏷️ **Marcus Gunn pupil** = RAPD [the Gun misfires] → 🎯 optic nerve (or severe retinal) disease; never a cataract
ck_dual.564: 🎬 **Droopy lid + small pupil + dry half-face** 🟰 🏷️ **Horner's syndrome** [Horns down] → 🎯 Pancoast tumour, carotid dissection

ck_add: 🎬 PR stretches longer, longer, longer… then a P wave with no QRS, and the cycle resets 🟰 🏷️ **Wenckebach = Mobitz I** [Weak Back: the PR box sags until it drops] → 🎯 usually benign: observe, stop AV-nodal drugs
Acute coronary syndrome / MI / unstable angina

🎬 Low BP + distended neck veins + quiet, distant heart sounds days after an MI or after chest trauma 🟰 🏷️ **Beck's triad** [Big neck veins, Beat muffled, BP low] → 🎯 **cardiac tamponade**: urgent echo + pericardiocentesis
🎬 Pressing the left iliac fossa makes the right iliac fossa hurt 🟰 🏷️ **Rovsing's sign** [Reverse: press left, hurts right] → 🎯 **appendicitis**

🎬 Short horizontal white lines at the lung edges above the costophrenic angles + big heart + upper lobe diversion 🟰 🏷️ **Kerley B lines** [Bars at the Base Borders] → 🎯 interstitial oedema: **heart failure**

🎬 Still blood (immobile, long flight) + sticky blood (cancer, pill, pregnancy) + a damaged vessel (surgery, trauma) 🟰 🏷️ **Virchow's triad** [3 V's: Velocity low, Vessel wall, Viscosity up] → 🎯 the recipe for **VTE**

🎬 A smoker with proximal leg weakness that briefly improves with repeated effort + dry mouth + absent reflexes 🟰 🏷️ **Lambert–Eaton syndrome** [Lift-Easier] → 🎯 **small cell** lung cancer (calcium channel antibodies)
🎬 Multiple, recurrent, distal duodenal ulcers + chronic diarrhoea, not healing on a standard PPI 🟰 🏷️ **Zollinger–Ellison syndrome** [Zillions of acid] → 🎯 **gastrinoma** (MEN1): fasting gastrin

🎬 Red, scaly, crusting patch that starts on the nipple tip and spreads to the areola, not settling with creams 🟰 🏷️ **Paget's disease of the nipple** [Patch on the Point] → 🎯 underlying cancer: **2WW** + punch biopsy
🎬 A man with buttock and thigh claudication + impotence + weak femoral pulses on both sides 🟰 🏷️ **Leriche syndrome** [Leg + Libido lost] → 🎯 **aortoiliac** occlusion
🎬 Veins emptied lying down, pressure on the groin, stand up: they stay empty until you let go 🟰 🏷️ **Trendelenburg test** [Tourniquet test] → 🎯 **saphenofemoral junction** reflux (confirm on duplex)

🎬 After thyroid surgery: a BP cuff cramps the hand into a claw and tapping the cheek twitches the mouth 🟰 🏷️ **Trousseau's** + **Chvostek's signs** [Tourniquet claw, Cheek-tap twitch] → 🎯 **hypocalcaemia**: IV calcium gluconate if severe

🎬 Hip flexed, straightening the knee hurts the back; lifting the head makes the hips and knees flex 🟰 🏷️ **Kernig's** + **Brudzinski's signs** [Knee; Bend neck, bend knees] → 🎯 poor sensitivity: a negative sign never rules out meningitis or delays antibiotics
🎬 A boy climbs up his own thighs with his hands to stand from the floor + bulky calves 🟰 🏷️ **Gowers' sign** [Go up the legs] → 🎯 proximal weakness: **Duchenne** (CK hugely raised)

🎬 Tapping the front of the wrist, or holding both wrists flexed for a minute, brings tingling into the thumb, index and middle fingers 🟰 🏷️ **Tinel's** + **Phalen's** [Tap-tingle; Fold-hand] → 🎯 **carpal tunnel** (median): splint, injection, decompression

🎬 A patient secretly injects insulin or contaminates urine samples just to be looked after as a patient 🟰 🏷️ **Munchausen syndrome** = factitious disorder [Baron of tall tales] → 🎯 intentional for the **sick role**: not malingering (money) and not unconscious
🎬 Scrape off the silvery scale and pinpoint bleeding spots appear underneath 🟰 🏷️ **Auspitz sign** [the plaque spits pinpoints of blood] → 🎯 **psoriasis**

🎬 The fork rings louder in air than on bone on both sides, but the forehead fork is louder in the good ear 🟰 🏷️ **Rinne positive** + **Weber** to the good side [Ring in the air; Web in the middle] → 🎯 **sensorineural** loss in the bad ear: MRI internal auditory meatus

🎬 The fork is louder on the bone than in the air on the bad side, and the forehead fork is louder in that same bad ear 🟰 🏷️ **Rinne negative** + **Weber** to the bad side [Ring in the air; Web in the middle] → 🎯 **conductive** loss: glue ear, wax, otosclerosis
